Use that first print only; ignore later revisions and do not add same-day correction or release-day grace exceptions.","dataPointId":"statcan.gdp_by_industry.monthly_growth.2026_11.first_print","historicalContext":[{"period":{"type":"month","value":"2026-03"},"label":"March 2026","value":-0.1521},{"period":{"type":"month","value":"2026-04"},"label":"April 2026","value":0.6326},{"period":{"type":"month","value":"2026-05"},"label":"May 2026","value":0.3415},{"period":{"type":"month","value":"2026-06"},"label":"June 2026","value":0.3512},{"period":{"type":"month","value":"2026-07"},"label":"July 2026","value":0.0258},{"period":{"type":"month","value":"2026-08"},"label":"August 2026","value":-0.0065}],"drivers":["Recent official monthly GDP growth averaged about 0.20% across March-August 2026 on current WDS levels.","Latest The Daily release says August was essentially unchanged and the advance September estimate was -0.1%.","Momentum is softer than the six-month mean, but November is two months beyond the last official print and likely mean-reverts toward small positive growth.","One-off industry rebounds in April-June raise historical volatility but are not assumed to persist into November."],"sourceContext":["https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorByReferencePeriodRange?vectorIds=%2265201210%22&startRefPeriod=2025-10-01&endReferencePeriod=2026-10-01","https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/release-diffusion/2026-eng.pdf","https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/daily-quotidien/261030/dq261030a-eng.htm","https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/13-607-x/2016001/v65201210-eng.htm"],"runAt":"2026-11-02T23:43:33Z","reasoning":[{"kind":"heading","text":"Canada November 2026 monthly GDP by industry first print"},{"kind":"text","text":"The target is the Statistics Canada all-industries GDP by industry level series v65201210, seasonally adjusted at annual rates, chained 2017 dollars, transformed to month-over-month percent growth for November 2026. I adjust downward for soft late-summer momentum and the -0.1% advance September signal, landing at 0.10% for November rather than the raw 0.20% mean. For the 80% interval, sigma = 0.2922 from call-0024 using the six growth values themselves; 1.28*sigma = 0.3740 from call-0026, so 0.10 +/- 0.374 gives -0.2740 to 0.4740, rounded to -0.27 to 0.47."},{"kind":"text","text":"Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanisms: the level trend is mildly positive over the six official observations, momentum is near flat after July-August and the advance September estimate, one-off rebounds in mining/manufacturing can move a monthly print but are not persistent, and there is no policy-decision mechanism in this data target."},{"kind":"text","text":"Upside risk is a broad rebound in goods sectors or resource extraction that would land above the interval.
